body:
@vvo

> Even that, for a first version I would put it on top and see what people are doing with it/needs.

I actually want the "Clear all" link after the list, I find it less logical to have it before the other ones. So I'm the one having the use-case. :)

@redox

> Regarding the "position" of the clear button, shouldn't that be a templating/layout customization rather than an option in the widget?

I agree, but I think we chose not too as soon as we started to expose `item`, `header`, `footer` templates instead of `body` ones. If we begin to expose the full template to chose the position, then we probably need to expose the full template for `refinementList` and everything, which means getting rid of `React` in the end in favor of templates + a custom made event API alongside.

> I think the clearSpecificRefinements should actually be an option of the refinementList widget; I don't think we want an extra widget for that.

Why not, but it means we'll need to add it to each and every one of the new widgets using facets. Are we sure we want to do this?
What if we want to put it in the header of the `refinementList` ?

> I also think we should just expose the allCurrentRefinementList, if the user wants to restrict to a single refinement, he could just pass an array of 1 element. I would also rename it to currentRefinementsList (plural).

Makes sense. Agreed. :+1:

> And if we go that way, I would then transform the clearAll widget to an option of the currentRefinementsList one.
> So at the end, it's a single currentRefinementsList widget + the addition of a clearAll option in that widget + refinementList one :) If the user doesn't want to see the list of refined values but just the "clear all button", he can set the templates.item to ''.

It already is an option of the big one.
About using the big one to display it, I strongly disagree though. First we'd be using un-needed resources to retrieve the list of refinements at each state update for nothing, and in

```js
  instantsearch.widgets.currentRefinementList({
    container: '#clear-all-link',
    templates: {
      item: ''
    },
    clearAll: true, // Will work as 'before'
    hideContainerWhenNoRefinements: true
  })
```

the name feels completely unrelated to the action to me.

I updated the main post to reflect these.
